mainTopic: The end of the סמפון discussion and the start of פרק אלו מציאות: which found items a finder keeps, and scattered produce
overview: This amud begins at the end of the גמרא's discussion of a סמפון, a receipt saying a loan was paid. The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying a receipt with witnesses is valid. It explains that this means עדי קיום, signatures already confirmed by בית דין, and proves this reading from the second half of the ברייתא. It then quotes the full ברייתא, which adds two more cases where a receipt is trusted: when a שליש held it, and when it is written on the loan document below the signatures. With the הדרן, the first פרק, שנים אוחזין, ends. The new פרק, אלו מציאות, opens with a משנה listing which found items the finder may keep and which he must announce. רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר give different views. The גמרא explains 'scattered produce' as one קב over four אמות, the case of grain dropped at the threshing floor that the owner gives up as הפקר. רבי ירמיה then asks a series of questions about whether the reason is the effort of gathering or the low value, and they end in תיקו. The amud closes with איתמר, opening a new teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: We can ask the witnesses whether the loan was paid
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: in that case we ask the witnesses whether the loan was repaid or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we ask the witnesses whether it was paid or whether it was not paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous discussion. In that case there is no problem, because we can go to the witnesses and ask them whether the debt was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since living witnesses are available, we do not need to rely on the paper alone. Their testimony settles whether the loan was paid, so the earlier challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses (Aramaic)
Paid, repaid (said of a debt)
We ask

phrases.english: since we ask the witnesses
whether it was paid or whether it was not paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a challenge raised before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution: the witnesses can be asked directly
steps.terutzMaskana: When witnesses are available, we ask them whether the debt was paid, so the earlier challenge does not apply.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a receipt with witnesses is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying a סמפון with witnesses on it is valid. It seems to say this without any conditions, even if the receipt is found with the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a receipt that has witnesses on it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge the view being discussed. The ברייתא says a סמפון with witnesses is valid, without saying where it was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא does not make any distinction, it seems to say the receipt is valid even if it turned up in the lender's possession. That would go against the view that such a receipt should not be trusted on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt or note stating that a debt (or part of it) was paid
Valid, can be relied upon
Witnesses whose signatures are on the document

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A receipt that has witnesses on it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: סִמְפּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After one challenge was answered, a new ברייתא is brought as a fresh challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a סמפון found with the lender is not automatically trusted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls a סמפון with witnesses valid and makes no distinction, so it seems valid wherever it is found.

steps.title: The witnesses are עדי קיום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about עדי קיום: the witnesses' signatures were confirmed by בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What witnesses does it mean? Witnesses of confirmation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining which witnesses the ברייתא means. It means witnesses whose signatures בית דין has already confirmed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A receipt confirmed by בית דין is valid no matter where it is found. So the ברייתא does not teach that any receipt with plain signatures is trusted, and the view under discussion still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses whose signatures were confirmed by בית דין, which makes the document fully established
What? Used to ask what a word in a source really means

phrases.english: What witnesses?
Witnesses of confirmation.
phrases.notes: These are witnesses whose signatures בית דין already checked and confirmed, so the receipt is backed by the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what a word in the source means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought 'witnesses' means any signatures at all, which would make every signed receipt valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Witnesses' means עדי קיום, so only a receipt confirmed by the court is automatically valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'עדים' here as ordinary signing witnesses. The גמרא's whole answer depends on reading it as עדי קיום, a receipt already confirmed by בית דין.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא supports reading it as עדי קיום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the end of the ברייתא makes sense only if 'witnesses' means עדי קיום. Otherwise the end would be saying something obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, since the end of the ברייתא says: 'and one that has no witnesses on it is invalid.' What does 'has no witnesses' mean? If you say it has no witnesses at all, does that even need to be said? Rather, it must mean it has no witnesses of confirmation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the second half of the same ברייתא. If 'no witnesses' meant no signatures at all, there would be no reason to say the receipt is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A receipt with no signatures at all is obviously worthless, and a ברייתא does not teach obvious things. So the end must mean a receipt that has signatures but was not confirmed by בית דין. That shows the beginning was talking about עדי קיום too.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense: support for the answer just given
The latter clause of a source
Invalid
Does it need to be said? Meaning it is too obvious to teach
Rather, is it not that: introduces the only reasonable reading

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
since it teaches in the latter clause:
and one that has no witnesses on it is invalid.
What does 'has no witnesses on it' mean?
If you say there are no witnesses on it at all,
does it need to be said that it is invalid?!
Rather, is it not about witnesses of confirmation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The reading of 'עדים' in the ברייתא as עדי קיום
steps.raayaSupportSource: The latter clause of the same ברייתא, which would be stating the obvious if it meant no signatures at all
steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, 'with witnesses' means confirmed by בית דין (עדי קיום). 'Without witnesses' means signed but not confirmed, and such a receipt is not automatically trusted.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: how a receipt is confirmed or made valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא in full. A receipt with witnesses is confirmed through its signers. A receipt without witnesses is still valid if it comes from a שליש, or if it was written after the signatures of the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: a receipt that has witnesses on it is confirmed through its signers. If it has no witnesses on it, but it comes out from the hands of a trustee, or it appears after the signatures of the documents, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא turns to study the ברייתא it quoted, now in its full wording. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא shows that a receipt with witnesses must be confirmed through those signers. It also adds two cases where even an unsigned receipt is valid. One is when a neutral trustee was holding it. The other is when the receipt was written on the loan document itself, below the witnesses' signatures.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא now studies a source it quoted earlier
It is confirmed through its signers, by checking the signatures
A neutral third party who holds a document for both sides
The signing of the documents, meaning the witnesses' signatures on the loan document

phrases.english: The matter itself.

phrases.aramaic: סִמְפּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים – יִתְקַיֵּים בְּחוֹתְמָיו.
phrases.english: A receipt that has witnesses on it is to be confirmed through its signers.
If it has no witnesses on it
but it comes out from the hands of a trustee,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁיּוֹצֵא לְאַחַר חִיתּוּם שְׁטָרוֹת – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: or it appears after the signing of the documents, it is valid.
phrases.notes: The receipt was written on the loan document itself, below the witnesses' signatures.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. סִמְפּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים – יִתְקַיֵּים בְּחוֹתְמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After using the ברייתא in a challenge, the גמרא now quotes and examines its full text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A receipt with witnesses is confirmed through its signers. A receipt without witnesses is valid if it comes from a שליש or appears after the signatures on the loan document.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא lists the ways a receipt can be trusted. The discussion that follows will analyze these cases.

steps.title: Why a receipt from a third party or after the signatures is trusted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the last two rulings of the ברייתא. A receipt held by a שליש is trusted because the lender trusted him. A receipt written after the signatures is trusted because no lender would damage his own document unless he had been paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the receipt comes out from a שליש, it is valid, because the lender trusted the שליש. If it comes out written after the signatures of the loan document, it is also valid, because if the loan had not been paid, the lender would never have weakened his own document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for each of the two cases in the ברייתא where a receipt with no witnesses is still accepted. This finishes the סמפון discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a receipt without witnesses is not trusted, since it could be fake. In the first case, the lender himself chose the שליש, so he cannot complain about what the שליש brings out. In the second case, the receipt is on the lender's own document, and a lender would not ruin his own document for no reason, so it must be true that he was paid.

keyTerms.meaning: A neutral third party who holds a document for both sides
He trusted him
The witnesses' signatures on the documents
That it (the loan) was repaid
Weakening or damaging his own document

steps.whatToRemember: A receipt without witnesses can still be trusted when the lender himself caused it to be trusted: either he gave it to a שליש he trusted, or he let it be written on his own loan document.

phrases.english: If it comes out from the hand of a third party, it is valid,
because the lender trusted the third party.
If it comes out after the signatures of the documents, it is also valid,
because if it had not been repaid,
he would not have weakened his own document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two cases in the ברייתא quoted in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A receipt from a שליש is trusted because the lender trusted the שליש. A receipt after the signatures is trusted because a lender would not damage his own document unless he had been paid.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing שנים אוחזין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the first פרק of בבא מציעא, שנים אוחזין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שנים אוחזין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. The first פרק of בבא מציעא is now complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the topics of this פרק are finished and shows our wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: said when finishing a פרק
Two are holding: the name of the first פרק of בבא מציעא

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Two are holding"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the סמפון discussion ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק, שנים אוחזין, is finished.

steps.title: New perek: which found items are kept and which must be announced
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens by saying there are two kinds of found items: ones the finder keeps, and ones he must announce.
steps.simpleTranslation: These found items belong to the finder, and for these he must announce that he found them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. The משנה sets up its topic by naming two groups of lost items, and it will spell out each group next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some found items go to the finder, and for others he must publicly announce the find so the owner can come and claim it. This opening line only names the two groups; the details come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Found items, lost objects that someone finds
To announce publicly that an item was found, so the owner can claim it

steps.whyThisMatters: This split between keeping and announcing is the main topic of the whole פרק אלו מציאות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These found items belong to him,
and for these he is obligated to announce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק with a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found items fall into two groups: some belong to the finder, and some must be announced.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's list of found items the finder may keep
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists found items the finder may keep: scattered produce and coins, bundles in a public place, fig cakes, baker's loaves, strings of fish, pieces of meat, wool fleeces, flax bundles and strips of purple wool. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: These found items belong to the finder: scattered produce, scattered coins, bundles of grain in a public place, round cakes of pressed figs, a baker's loaves, strings of fish, pieces of meat, wool fleeces straight from where they were sheared, bundles of flax, and strips of purple wool. These belong to him. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now fills in the first group from the opening line: the items a finder may keep. The list is said in the name of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these items look like many others of the same kind, so the owner has no way to prove they are his. That is why the finder keeps them. Naming רבי מאיר tells us other תנאים may disagree, and the משנה goes on to bring רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Scattered, lying here and there
Bundles or sheaves of grain
A public area
Round cakes of pressed figs
A baker
Purple-dyed wool

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the finder keeps these just because they are cheap. As the next part of the משנה shows with רבי יהודה, the issue is whether the item has something special about it that lets the owner identify it.

phrases.english: These found items belong to him:
if he found scattered produce,
scattered coins,
bundles of grain in a public area,
and round cakes of pressed figs,
loaves of a baker,
strings of fish,
and pieces of meat,
and wool fleeces taken from their place of origin,
phrases.notes: He means raw wool brought straight from the shearing, before anyone has worked on it.

phrases.english: and bundles of flax stalks,
and strips of purple wool —
these belong to him,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ מְצִיאוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ: מָצָא פֵּירוֹת מְפוּזָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first group named in Step 8, the items that belong to the finder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a finder may keep scattered produce and coins, bundles in a public area, fig cakes, baker's loaves, strings of fish, pieces of meat, raw wool fleeces, flax bundles and strips of purple wool.

steps.title: An item with an unusual feature must be announced
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that any found item with something unusual about it must be announced, and he gives two examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: anything that has something unusual about it must be announced. For example, a fig cake with a piece of pottery inside it, or a loaf with coins inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהודה, who adds a limit to the list of items a finder may keep. If an item has something unusual about it, the finder must announce it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary fig cake or loaf has no way to identify its owner, so the finder may keep it. But a piece of pottery or coins inside it is an unusual feature, and the owner can name it as a sign. So the item now has a way back to its owner, and the finder must announce it.

keyTerms.meaning: Something unusual or different about the item
To announce the find publicly
A round cake of pressed figs
A piece of broken pottery
Coins

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שִׁינּוּי – חַיָּיב לְהַכְרִיז.
phrases.english: Anything that has something unusual about it must be announced.
How so?
If he found a round fig cake with a piece of pottery inside it,
or a loaf with coins inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שִׁינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי מאיר's list of items the finder may keep
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any found item with an unusual feature must be announced.

steps.title: אנפוריא vessels do not need to be announced
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rules that a finder never has to announce אנפוריא vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: for all אנפוריא vessels, the finder does not need to announce them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a third view, from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. A certain kind of vessel, called אנפוריא, never needs to be announced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels usually have to be announced, because an owner can describe them. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר carves out a category of vessels that the finder may keep. The גמרא will later explain what these vessels are.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of vessel that the finder may keep (the גמרא explains the term later)
He is not obligated

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three views. רבי מאיר lists items with no sign that the finder keeps. רבי יהודה says anything with an unusual feature must be announced. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says אנפוריא vessels never need announcing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
all anpurya vessels,
he is not obligated to announce them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל כְּלֵי אַנְפּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the משנה, adding a group of items the finder may keep
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder does not need to announce אנפוריא vessels.

steps.title: How much produce counts as scattered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting 'scattered produce' from the משנה and asks how much counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said, 'If he found scattered produce.' How much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It picks up the first case on רבי מאיר's list and asks for a measurement. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only 'scattered,' without saying how spread out the produce must be. The גמרא wants a clear amount for a given area, so we know when the finder may keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Scattered produce
And how much?

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'If he found scattered produce.'
And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's first case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much produce, spread over what area, counts as 'scattered'

steps.title: One קב spread over four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that produce counts as scattered when one קב is spread over four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: one קב spread over four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives the measurement. One קב of produce spread over an area of four אמות counts as scattered, so the finder may keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer ties the rule to a ratio, an amount within an area. If the produce is spread this thin, it counts as 'scattered' in the sense of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume for dry produce
Four cubits (an area of four by four cubits)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
One kav in four cubits.
phrases.notes: He means one קב spread over a four-by-four cubit area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: קַב בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One קב in an area of four אמות counts as scattered produce.

steps.title: Why should the amount matter at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק. If the produce fell, the finder should keep any amount. If it was put down, he should keep none.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it looks like it fell, then even more produce should also be his. If it looks like it was put down on purpose, then even less produce should still not be his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק's measurement. It argues that what should decide the law is how the produce got there, not how much there is. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce that fell by accident has no sign, so the owner has given up on it, and the amount should not matter. Produce that was put down on purpose means the owner plans to come back, so even a small amount should not be taken. Either way, the measurement 'one קב in four אמות' seems to play no role.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (asks for the exact situation)
In a way that shows it fell by accident
In a way that shows it was placed on purpose
A lot, more
Less than this

steps.confusionAlert: 'הֵיכִי דָּמֵי' looks like a simple question, but here it works as a challenge. The גמרא is saying the measurement does not seem to fit either possible case.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If it is in a way that shows it fell,
then even a larger amount should also be his!
And if it is in a way that shows it was placed there,
then even less than this should also not be his!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the measurement given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's measurement of one קב in four אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whether the finder may keep the produce depends on whether it fell or was placed, not on the amount. So the measurement seems pointless in both cases.

steps.title: The case is produce dropped at the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא answers the challenge against רבי יצחק. The case is grain that fell at the threshing floor during gathering. One קב over four אמות is too much bother, so the owner gives it up. Anything less, he comes back for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא said: We are dealing with the gathering at the threshing floors. When one קב is spread over four אמות, collecting it is a lot of work. A person won't bother to come back and take it, so he gives it up as ownerless. When it is less spread out than that, he does bother to come back and take it, so he does not give it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 14. It explains why the amount and the spread of the produce decide who keeps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that dropped produce is either always lost or never lost, so a measurement makes no sense. רב עוקבא answers that the produce did fall by accident, but the owner's attitude depends on the effort involved. A קב over four אמות is too much bother, so he gives it up (הפקר). Anything less spread out is worth coming back for, so he does not give it up.

keyTerms.meaning: The gathering of grain at the threshing floors
Collecting them takes a lot of effort
He fully gives it up as ownerless (הֶפְקֵר)
Less than this

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of scattered produce works through הפקר. One קב over four אמות is too much bother to collect, so the owner gives it up and the finder may keep it.

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Chama said:
We are dealing with the gathering at the threshing floors.
phrases.notes: He means grain that dropped by accident while it was being gathered in at harvest time.

phrases.english: A kav over four cubits, where collecting it is a lot of work:
phrases.notes: Four אמות here means an area of four by four אמות.

phrases.english: a person does not bother and does not go back
to come and take them,
so he gives them up as ownerless.
Less than this:
he bothers and goes back, comes and takes them,
and he does not give them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: בְּמַכְנַשְׁתָּא דְּבֵי דָרֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 14 by defining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dropped produce is either always lost or never lost, so a measurement makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce fell by accident at the threshing floor. The owner gives it up only when collecting it is too much bother, meaning a קב over four אמות.

steps.title: Half a קב over two אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about half a קב spread over two אמות. The answer depends on why the owner gives up a קב over four אמות. Is it because of the effort, or because it is not worth much?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: What is the law for half a קב over two אמות? Why does the owner give up a קב over four אמות? If it is because collecting it is a lot of work, then half a קב over two אמות is not much work, so he does not give it up. Or perhaps it is because it is not worth much. Then half a קב over two אמות is also not worth much, so he gives it up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question (a בעיא). He wants to know which reason is behind the rule of step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half a קב over two אמות is spread just as thinly as a קב over four, but the total amount is smaller. If the reason is effort, a smaller area means less work, so the owner keeps his claim. If the reason is low value, half a קב is worth even less, so he gives it up.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (בַּעְיָא) that may stay unresolved
Half a קב (a dry measure)
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the question)
They are not worth much (not significant)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Half a kav over two cubits, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Two אמות here means an area of two by four, so it is half the size of the four-by-four area.

phrases.english: A kav over four cubits, what is the reason?
Because collecting them is a lot of work.
Then half a kav over two cubits,
since collecting them is not a lot of work,
he does not give them up.
Or perhaps it is because they are not worth much,
and half a kav over two cubits,
since they are not worth much, he gives them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: חֲצִי קַב בִּשְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב עוקבא's rule and asks which reason is behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason for הפקר the large effort or the low value? Half a קב over two אמות tests the difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is found. In step 21 the גמרא ends the whole series with תיקו.

steps.title: Two קבין over eight אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about two קבין spread over eight אמות. If the reason is effort, this is even more work, so the owner gives it up. If the reason is low value, two קבין are worth something, so he keeps his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for two קבין over eight אמות? Why does the owner give up a קב over four אמות? If it is because collecting it is a lot of work, then two קבין over eight אמות are even more work, so he certainly gives them up. Or perhaps it is because a קב is not worth much. Then two קבין are worth something, so he does not give them up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a second question that tests the same two reasons from the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case flips step 16. Here the area and the amount both grow. Under the effort reason the owner gives it up all the more (כל שכן). Under the low-value reason the larger amount is worth something, so he does not give it up.

keyTerms.meaning: Two קבין
All the more so
More
They are worth something (significant)

phrases.english: Two kav over eight cubits, what is the law?
A kav over four cubits, what is the reason?
Because collecting them is a lot of work,
and all the more so two kav over eight cubits,
since collecting them is even more work,
he gives them up.
Or perhaps it is because they are not worth much,
and two kav over eight cubits,
since they are worth something, he does not give them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question in the same series, testing the two reasons in the opposite direction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: With a larger amount over a larger area, does the extra effort lead to הפקר, or does the higher value prevent it?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is found. In step 21 the גמרא ends the whole series with תיקו.

steps.title: A קב of sesame seeds over four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a קב of sesame over four אמות. Sesame is worth more than grain but is harder to pick up. So the two reasons give opposite answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a קב of sesame over four אמות? Why does the owner give up a קב over four אמות? If it is because grain is not worth much, then sesame is worth something, so he does not give it up. Or perhaps it is because collecting it is a lot of work. Then sesame is all the more work, so he gives it up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a third question. This time the amount and the area stay the same, and only the type of produce changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sesame seeds are valuable but tiny, so they are very hard to collect. Under the low-value reason, sesame keeps the owner's claim. Under the effort reason, the owner gives sesame up even more readily than grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Sesame seeds (small and valuable)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that in this question the order of the two sides is switched: the low-value reason comes first and the effort reason second. In every one of these questions, the two reasons point to opposite results.

phrases.english: A kav of sesame over four cubits, what is the law?
A kav over four cubits, what is the reason?
Because they are not worth much,
and sesame, since it is worth something,
he does not give it up.
Or perhaps it is because collecting them is a lot of work,
and all the more so sesame,
since collecting it is even more work,
he gives it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third question in the same series. Here the type of produce changes instead of the amount.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: For produce that is valuable but hard to collect, which reason decides: effort or value?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is found. In step 21 the גמרא ends the whole series with תיקו.

steps.title: A קב of dates or pomegranates over four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a קב of dates or pomegranates spread over four אמות. If the owner gives up a קב of grain because it is not worth much, he gives these up too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a קב of dates over four אמות, or a קב of pomegranates over four אמות? Why does the owner give up a קב over four אמות? If it is because it is not worth much, then a קב of dates or pomegranates is also not worth much, so he gives them up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks another question about the same rule, now with dates and pomegranates. The גמרא first lays out one side: if the reason is low value, the owner gives these fruits up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tests the same two reasons as steps 16-18, low value or effort. Under the low-value reason, a קב of dates or pomegranates counts the same as a קב of grain. It is not worth much, so the owner gives it up.

keyTerms.meaning: dates
pomegranates
what is the reason?
worth something, important
he gives them up as ownerless (הפקר)

phrases.english: A kav of dates spread over four amos,
a kav of pomegranates spread over four amos, what is the law?
A kav over four amos, what is the reason he gives it up?
Because they are not worth much.
Then a kav of dates over four amos,
and a kav of pomegranates over four amos too,
since they are not worth much, he gives them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַב תַּמְרֵי בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, קַב רִמּוֹנֵי בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case in רבי ירמיה's series of questions testing the reason behind the rule of a קב over four אמות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an owner give up a קב of dates or pomegranates scattered over four אמות?

steps.title: The other side: big fruits are easy to collect
steps.stepSummary: If the owner gives up the grain because picking it up is too much work, dates and pomegranates are easy to collect. So he would not give them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the owner gives up a קב of grain over four אמות because it takes a lot of effort to collect. A קב of dates or pomegranates over four אמות does not take much effort, so he does not give them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite side of רבי ירמיה's question. If the reason is effort, the owner keeps his claim to the dates and pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small grain kernels scattered over four אמות are hard to gather one by one. Dates and pomegranates are large pieces, so a קב of them is quick to pick up. Under the effort reason, the owner does not give them up, which is the opposite of step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
the effort they require
is great, is a lot

phrases.english: Or perhaps he gives it up because the effort to collect them is great,
phrases.notes: "Them" here means the scattered grain kernels from the original case.

phrases.english: and a kav of dates over four amos,
and a kav of pomegranates over four amos,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא נְפִישׁ טִרְחַיְיהוּ – לָא מַפְקַר לְהוּ.
phrases.english: since the effort to collect them is not great, he does not give them up.
phrases.notes: Dates and pomegranates are big pieces, so picking them up is quick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the same question, which leads to the opposite answer

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is and answers תיקו. רבי ירמיה's questions stay unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? It stays undecided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי ירמיה's questions by saying תיקו. Nobody can prove which reason is correct, so the questions are left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of רבי ירמיה's questions depend on one thing: is the reason low value or effort? The גמרא cannot settle that, so none of the cases (steps 16-20) gets a final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: what (is the law)?
let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: An owner gives up a קב of grain scattered over four אמות. We do not know whether that is because it is not worth much or because it is too much work to gather, so רבי ירמיה's questions stay as תיקו.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is no. It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: What is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
phrases.notes: This applies to all of רבי ירמיה's questions, not just the last one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole series of רבי ירמיה's questions
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reason behind the rule of a קב over four אמות is left undecided, so all of רבי ירמיה's questions remain תיקו.

steps.title: A new teaching is introduced
steps.stepSummary: The word איתמר opens a new teaching quoted from the אמוראים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a new statement or argument of the אמוראים, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איתמר does not say anything by itself. It marks the start of a new section of the סוגיא about lost objects and an owner giving up hope.

keyTerms.meaning: an owner giving up hope of getting his item back, the main idea behind this sugya

phrases.english: It was stated:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after the תיקו closed רבי ירמיה's questions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a new statement of the אמוראים that follows.
